Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese deitar, from Vulgar Latin *dēctāre, from Latin dējectāre, frequentative of dējicere (“to throw, hurl down”). Compare Portuguese deitar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /dejˈtaɾ/

Verb

[edit]

deitar (first-person singular present deito, first-person singular preterite deitei, past participle deitado)

  1. (transitive) to lay; to lean
    Synonym: pousar
    • c. 1295, R. Lorenzo, editor, La traducción gallega de la Crónica General y de la Crónica de Castilla, Ourense: I.E.O.P.F, page 806:
      prouarõ tres escaleyras de fuste et acharõnas curtas; et desi atarõnas a hũa cõ a outra et deytarõnas a hũa torre
      they tried three wooden ladders but found them too short; and so they tied them together and leaned them against a tower
  2. (transitive) to cause to fall
  3. (pronominal) to lie down
  4. (transitive) to throw; to expel
    Synonym: chimpar
  5. (transitive) to pour
    Synonym: botar
  6. (transitive) to leak
    Synonym: perder

Old Galician-Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • deitare

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin dējectāre, frequentative of dējicere (“to throw, hurl down”), probably via an early *deieitar, with reduction via haplology.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /dej.ˈtaɾ/
  • Rhymes: -aɾ

Verb

[edit]

deitar

  1. to lay (to place down in a position of rest, or in a horizontal position)
    • a. 1284, Alfonso X of Castile, Cantigas de Santa Maria, Códice de los músicos, cantiga 4 (facsimile):
      Eſta e como Santa maria guardou ao fillo do judeu que non ardeſſe que ſeu padre deitara no forno
      This one is about how Holy Mary protected from being burnt the son of the Jew whose father had been laid in the furnace.

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese deitar, from a Vulgar Latin *dēctāre, from Latin dējectāre,[1][2][3] frequentative of dējicere (“to throw, hurl down”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /dejˈta(ʁ)/ [deɪ̯ˈta(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /dejˈta(ʁ)/ [deɪ̯ˈta(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /dejˈta(ɾ)/ [deɪ̯ˈta(ɾ)]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /dejˈta(ʁ)/ [deɪ̯ˈta(χ)]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /dejˈta(ɻ)/ [deɪ̯ˈta(ɻ)]
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /dɐjˈtaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /dɐjˈtaɾ/
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /dejˈtaɾ/
    • (Central Portugal) IPA(key): /dejˈtaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /deˈta.ɾi/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: dei‧tar

Verb

[edit]

deitar (first-person singular present deito, first-person singular preterite deitei, past participle deitado)

  2. (intransitive, sometimes pronominal) to lie down (to rest in a horizontal position)
    Synonym: reclinar(-se)
    Antonyms: erguer-se, levantar
  4. (by extension, intransitive) to go to sleep
    Synonym: ir dormir
  6. (transitive) to lay (to place in a horizontal position)
  8. (transitive) to throw [with direct object ‘something’, along with a or em ‘to someone’]
    Synonyms: arremessar, jogar, lançar, tacar
    deitar fora ― to throw away
  10. (transitive) to pour [with direct object ‘something’ and sobre ‘onto something’]
  12. (transitive) to emit; to give off; to give out
    Synonym: emitir
  13. (reflexive) to drop (to lower oneself quickly to the ground)
  14. (reflexive) to lie down (to assume a reclining position)
